A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph-power fusion work, with LEGO renamed EGO. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original video anomaly detection experiments on four datasets, including fusion comparisons, hyperparameter evaluations and graph visualizations in Tables 1-3 and Figures 3-7.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds large-dataset comparisons, timing measurements, noise experiments and cross-dataset evaluations in Appendices I-K.

M1.justification: The relationship graphs, graph-power expansion, learnable fusion operator, random pairwise sampling, degree-variance regularization and classification procedure remain unchanged. LEGO-to-EGO renaming and expressing classifier dimensions through N, still set to 32, do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual evaluations on XD-Violence, UCF-Crime and MSAD beyond the original four datasets. Appendix K also introduces corrupted-text inputs and testing on datasets excluded from training; the latter differs from v1's joint ShanghaiTech/Ped2 training.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained elementary fusion methods and MTN, v3 adds reported MSAD comparisons with MIST, UR-DMU and MGFN in Table 5, and RTFM in Tables 6-7. He et al. and Yu et al. are discussed but are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include XD-Violence AP, MSAD Protocol ii with AUC/AP breakdowns, 10/30/50% Gaussian-noise conditions with separate training/testing controls, and ShanghaiTech-only training followed by five-dataset transfer testing. Appendix J adds per-video V100 timing alongside retained per-epoch RTX 4070 measurements. Table 3 also changes ShanghaiTech's reported n from 3 to 6, without establishing whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds performance breakdowns across 11 MSAD anomaly types and 14 scenarios, controlled noise robustness tests, and cross-dataset generalization analysis. Original sensitivity plots and graph examples remain. Table 10 repeats feature-combination results already in v1 Table 2; its robustness interpretation is new, but those results are not.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates; v3 Table 8 introduces plus/minus quantities for training and testing times. Their statistical meaning and repetition counts are unspecified. Detection scores remain point estimates, and neither additional seeds nor an increased number of runs can be inferred.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1-2 and Table 3 AUC values are retained, while substantial results are added. Table 4 reports EGO at 65.77 AP versus MTN's 77.17 on XD-Violence, and 81.71 AUC versus 85.14 on UCF-Crime. Table 5 reports 87.36 on MSAD. Further tables add subgroup scores, timings, noise responses and transfer results; Table 10 duplicates existing scores.

T1.justification: Appendix I adds computational-complexity reasoning, asserting O(N^2.37) serial matrix multiplication, O(log N) on GPUs and O((P+Q) log N) graph expansion. No proof or processor-scaling assumptions substantiate the parallel bound. Existing Equations 1-9 and the distance/similarity and fusion-operator derivations are retained.

C1.justification: Apart from naming, the abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: relationship-centric fusion, learned integration of graph powers, a polynomial connection, and effective, efficient, interpretable video anomaly detection. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: New appendices substantially expand interpretations of real-world multi-hop relationships, scalability, noise suppression through degree-variance regularization, feature quality and cross-dataset generalization. These interpretations remain insufficiently qualified: strong generalization language accompanies low transfer AUCs, and the claimed noise degradation within 2% conflicts with Table 9's decline from 97.26 to 94.86.

D1.justification: v3 documents OpenPose/ST-GCN pose processing, SwinT's 1024-dimensional features, 30-50 training epochs, and the V100/batch-size-32 timing setup. Pose and SwinT results already existed, so these disclosures do not establish changed extractors. Conversely, v3 drops v1's ResNet-50 and supervised-SimCSE qualifiers. No code-access improvement is documented.

R1.justification: v3 adds specific positioning against He et al.'s cross-graph attention and Yu et al.'s graph-based retrieval, plus references supporting encoders, new comparators and complexity claims. The main Related Work section remains essentially unchanged. Zhu et al.'s publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: LEGO becomes EGO, the title loses its acronym prefix, and short setup and hyperparameter passages are edited. Five appendix sections are inserted before the existing visualizations, now Appendix L instead of G. The main narrative, section sequence and most existing prose remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds eight appendix tables, including extensive anomaly/scenario breakdowns and timing, noise and transfer displays. Table 10 redisplays original Table 2 results. Figures 1-7 are retained, with the final visualizations relocated to Appendix L; original table labels, Table 3 placement/caption and publication headers receive smaller presentation changes.

improvement.justification: Broader benchmarks, additional comparators, controlled noise/transfer tests and clearer implementation details make v3 more informative and expose applicability limits absent from v1. The gain is constrained by overinterpretation: Table 4 shows losses to MTN, four of five transfer AUCs in Table 11 are below 50, and Table 9 contradicts the stated 2% robustness bound. These additions improve empirical scrutiny, but the conclusions do not adequately reflect the mixed evidence.
